scope: Read-only source/spec/caller review and real producer probes for alerts5149/129; no HTML browser/rendering sink claim.

5149.observation: Ordinary script close control stripped; legal close whitespace variant retained byte-identically in direct string and nested list/dict output.
5149.limitation: No downstream HTML-rendering exploit demonstrated; public sanitizer itself makes security claim.

129.classification: XSS not reproduced at text producer; actual extraction correctness bug
129.observation: DocumentProcessorNode.execute returns alert(1), no raw HTML tags, for closing-space script; returns empty for ordinary control. Style close-space similarly leaves non-visible CSS in extracted text.
129.limitation: Final tag stripping and heading regex constrain tested output; metadata file paths and arbitrary downstream rendering are outside this finding. Do not generalize to universal HTML sanitizer security.

proposal: Document extraction: parser-based script/style exclusion with preserved heading/text outputs, malformed/unclosed and closing-whitespace tests.

Trust metadata: decide and document rendering contract before adopting broad escaping/markup deletion; use parser-aware sanitization or text-only escaped output, preserve benign data/containers and assert keys+values recursion.
Do not claim adding whitespace to current regex establishes complete HTML safety; unclosed script/source markup and nested deletion fusion require explicit tests.
